claims.text: The initial HfNbTaTiZr alloy is a chemically disordered, single-phase BCC solid solution.
Atomic size mismatch produces severe local lattice distortion in HfNbTaTiZr.
The low lattice thermal conductivity of random HfNbTaTiZr is dominated by phonon scattering from random atomic disorder.
Controlled annealing or thermal history can induce HfTi and TiZr short-range ordering in HfNbTaTiZr.
HfTi and TiZr short-range order develops into ordered B2-like clusters that can form a percolating network.
Ordering and clustering can drive multicomponent alloys from disordered solid solutions toward ordered or multiphase microstructures.
Coherent ordered B2-like HfTi and TiZr clusters locally reduce RMS atomic displacement relative to the random HfNbTaTiZr alloy.
Ordered B2-like clusters create percolative pathways for high-frequency phonons.
Ordered/disordered phase boundaries scatter phonons and tend to reduce lattice thermal conductivity.
B2 ordering in HfNbTaTiZr relaxes atomic-size-mismatch strain fields and reduces the scattering cross-section for high-frequency phonons.
Once the ordered clusters percolate, their low-scattering channels dominate heat transport over interface scattering.
A percolated SRO state has higher lattice thermal conductivity than the random HfNbTaTiZr state.
The conductivity increase is accompanied by higher group velocities in the high-frequency phonon spectrum.
The percolated state exhibits narrower high-frequency phonon-mode FWHM, indicating longer phonon lifetimes.
Below the cluster percolation threshold, interface scattering prevents the proposed conductivity enhancement.
At sufficiently high temperature the B2-like clusters dissolve, whereas at sufficiently low temperature diffusion kinetics prevent percolation.
The conductivity-enhancement mechanism requires the ordered phase to have less lattice distortion than the random solid solution.
